title: Swap one accent word in place
statement: Keep a fixed sentence and swap only its last word or number in place in the accent colour, or land a typed sentence on a one-word accent answer.
evidence: Four round-3 pieces (one tier A) swap an accent word; a tier-B round-6 film lands a typed sentence on a one-word accent answer.

title: Captions: 42 chars, 2 lines, 20 cps
statement: Captions keep <= 42 characters per line, <= 2 lines and <= 20 characters/s (17 for kids) with 2-frame gaps; a burned 9:16 track at 64 px re-breaks to 23 characters; faster speech is condensed by hand.
evidence: Standards table of the access lane; a multi-voice cold open measured 31-41 cps (0.8 s per voice) and fails honestly.

sources.locator: Shared-file edits NEEDED item 2-3; Findings for other lanes; RECIPE D

notes: plan.chunkCaptions (<= 4 words, <= 22 chars) is the stricter burned-caption chunker for short-form. | Merged: Subtitle files keep at most 42 characters a line, 2 lines, 20 cps (17 for kids) and 5/6 s to 7 s per event; burned-in kinetic captions keep at most 18 characters a line and 2 lines, with the active word exactly the spoken word. [house; house caption limits.] | plan.chunkCaptions defaults to <= 4 words / <= 22 chars, lead 2 frames; RECIPE H asks for 2-4 word captions at 64-80 px on 9:16; structure_check cps_max 17.

title: Captions: 2 lines, 18 chars
statement: Vertical captions are 64-80 px at 1080, at most 2 lines of at most 18 characters, 2-4 words per chunk, with the active word highlighted being exactly the spoken word; 16:9 captions are at least 40 px.
evidence: pack caption rules coded in lintCaptionStyle and lintCaptions; eyes applies the caption floor and 80 px cap.
notes: Tools that touch it today: type/captions.js lintCaptions (called in templates/_shared/human/edit.mjs). Set today by: templates/talking-head config.mjs captions.maxWords 3, maxChars 15 (a pack default outside mp plan). | Conflict: templates/_shared/plan.mjs chunkCaptions defaults to maxChars 22 per chunk, which can exceed 18 characters on one line; the talking-head template is stricter (3 words, 15 chars).

title: Caption every spoken sentence
statement: Every spoken sentence has a caption so the video works on mute; burn captions in for X and LinkedIn, which autoplay muted.
evidence: house rule R14; sound-on is dominant on YouTube (95%, second-hand) but feeds autoplay muted.
notes: tools/captions/validate.py validates a caption track; nothing checks that every spoken sentence has one. | lint_shotlist only warns on a missing sound_off sentence; burn with tools/captions/export.py --burn (no libass in many ffmpeg builds). | Merged: Every spoken phrase is burned in as a caption (lower-third box) so a VO film plays on mute. [measured; Round-8 film 03 (boosted-looking, 1.86M views) captions every phrase; the tier-A founder film instead relies on UI text.]

title: Cap caption emphasis scale at 1.05
statement: An emphasised caption word scales <= 1.05 while word gaps come from unscaled widths; at 1.12 it eats the 0.28 em gap and two words fuse.
evidence: A vlog sheet showed two caption words fused at scale 1.12; the template now overrides to 1.05.

sources.locator: Findings outside this lane, captions bullet

notes: Set today by: templates/vlog-personal/config.mjs captions.override.emphScale 1.05 (a pack default outside mp plan). | The real fix (gap from the scaled width) belongs in type/dom.js; other templates still use the 1.12 style default.

title: Exits 30% faster than entrances
statement: Type entrances decelerate and exits accelerate, with exits about 30% shorter than entrances (e.g. lower third in 10-18 f, out 8-10 f).
evidence: type-module rule baked into the preset and gfx durations.
notes: Set today by: type/presets.js PRESETS durations; type/gfx/editorial.js inF/outF (a pack default outside mp plan). | lintType does not test exit speed; the presets set it.

title: Type size floors per role
statement: At the 1080 reference (shorter side) text is at least: read line 48 px wide / 56 px tall, headline 96, caption 40 / 64 (max 80 tall), label and end-card fine print 28 / 30, lower third 44 / 48, in-world 28; and at least 9 px when rendered on a 360 px wide phone.
evidence: house defaults set after reviewers could not read smaller text on a phone; eyes and a11y/text-size fail text below the floor.

sources.locator: Findings for other lanes, first bullet
Known weak spots > eyes, readability and safe zones

notes: Under 12 px on a 360 px phone is a note (the size a tested 16:9 table needed). Measurement needs plan.texts with fontPx. | Merged: Text meets the floors at 1080 (read 48 px wide / 56 px tall, headline 96, caption 40/64, label 28/30) and reads on a 360 px wide still at >= 9 px with contrast >= 4.5:1. [house; house floors; WCAG contrast.] | Also tools/a11y_check.py text-size. Real UI at scale 1 is too small on 16:9: use scale 1.3-1.6. | Merged: Headlines are >= 96 px on wide frames, reading text >= 48 px wide / 56 px tall at the 1080 reference, and no text renders under 9 px on a 360 px phone. [measured; Feature-drop headlines measured 76-92 px with a tag at 8.2 px on a 360 px phone (eyes, both runs); two device templates set reading text at 44 px on 16:9 (a11y_check fail).] | a11y/text-size checks the plan before the render. The fix for the feature drop moves its window layout, so it stayed open.

title: Honesty labels readable, 2 s
statement: Honesty labels are a designed component: mono family, at least 28 px (16:9) or 30 px (9:16), at least 4.5:1, inside the safe area, on screen at least 2 s, in a constant position across shots and never over the hero.
evidence: pack honesty-label style; eyes fails a label under 2 s and the storyboard checks the hold.
notes: Tools that touch it today: storyboard/label-hold. Set today by: design.json frames.labels.min_on_screen_s (a pack default outside mp plan). | Keep one label vocabulary across a series.

title: Accent the one key word
statement: Use 1-2 short lines per card and mark the key word in each line with the single accent colour or a highlight chip.
evidence: 2 of 3 tier-A films: an accent-colour word per line in one; a highlight chip behind key words in the other.

title: Lower third: name, title, 2.5-4 s
statement: A lower third shows name and title only, sits inside the platform safe rect, stays on screen about 2.5-4 s, and uses the accent on one element only.
evidence: pack special-frame rule; the lower-third parts default to 3 s (news bar 4 s).
notes: Set today by: design.json frames.lower_third (a pack default outside mp plan). | docs/evidence/visual.md gives a hold of at least 60 f (2 s) with bar wipe 10 f, name slide 12 f offset 4 f, out 8 f; frame-design's 2.5-4 s is kept.

title: Give each name super one personal detail
statement: In a multi-voice documentary, hold names until the lead, and give each later name super one personal detail beyond the role.
evidence: One tier-A round-4 launch documentary (153 s, 3.23x).

title: Signal, do not repeat the voice
statement: Explainers and tutorials put keyword callouts and step cards on screen, not sentences that repeat the narration.
evidence: A multimedia-learning handbook review: on-screen text duplicating narration hurt learning in 16 of 16 tests (median d = 0.86); signalling helped in 24 of 28 (d = 0.41).

sources.locator: 1. The fifteen findings, row 9; 4. On-screen text density

notes: Accessibility captions are separate and still required for mute viewing.

title: Never let two text boxes overlap
statement: No two on-screen text boxes overlap on any frame; the caption row keeps its own band and lower thirds and speaker tags sit above it.
evidence: Contact sheets of the 19 Oct run showed 5 collisions: a caption row over a lower third at 2.95 and 3.46 s, captions over a speaker tag on most talking frames, a label under a spec number at 19.2 s, port labels overlapping at 34.8 s, a feature line over the watermark at 9.2 s.

sources.locator: Known weak spots > Label collisions seen on the sheets

notes: eyes/safezones tests each box against the safe rect, not boxes against each other; found only by looking at sheets.

title: One kinetic type style
statement: A piece uses one kinetic-type tone family, two at most, chosen from the tone cell (calm-soft, calm-sharp, kinetic-soft, kinetic-sharp, neutral).
evidence: type-module rule coded in lintPiece; presets are tagged with the same tone cells frame-design picks.
notes: Tools that touch it today: type/presets.js lintPiece. Set today by: design.json tone.cell, motion.type_presets (a pack default outside mp plan). | lintPiece is a library lint, called only by templates/demo-l7/make.mjs; no build gate runs it.

title: Speak in 2-5 word phrases
statement: A wordless film carries its whole argument in on-screen phrases of 2-5 words, one phrase per beat.
evidence: All 6 wordless round-8 films do this (4 of them tier A on small samples); the round-7 hardware film's supers are 2-3 words.

sources.locator: Beat tables: the four tier-A films (film 04)

notes: Tools that touch it today: eyes/readability. | eyes/readability caps a read at 6 words; the 2-word floor is not checked.

title: Six words per read line
statement: Each shot carries one read line of at most 6 words; a hook line at most 7 words; a poster or cover at most 4.
evidence: pack type rules checked by eyes on the plan's texts and by the story linter on the shot list.
notes: Tools that touch it today: lint_shotlist.hook_max_words. Set today by: design.json type.max_words_per_line (a pack default outside mp plan).

title: Hold text long enough to read
statement: Hold each line for max(0.5 s, 0.35 s + 0.28 s per word), keep reading speed at or under 3.5 words per second, and show every line fully formed for at least 9 frames.
evidence: type-module rules; eyes fails text on screen for less than the formula (warns from 80%), lintType flags holds under 9 f.
notes: Tools that touch it today: a11y/reading-time; structure_check.check_text. | Captions that follow the voice only warn, never fail. | Merged: Non-speech on-screen text runs at most 3.5 words/s and holds at least max(0.5 s, 0.35 s + 0.28 s per word); the beat-sheet floor max(0.83 s, 0.3 s per word) also applies and the longer hold wins. Kinetic type holds each line fully formed for at least 9 frames and uses at most two tone families. [house; house reading formula shared by eyes, frame-design and story-script.] | Also lint_shotlist (hold 0.35+0.28/word) and structure_check.check_text (floor max(0.833, 0.3 s/word)). check_text one_word_frames 9 covers the formed hold; judge legibility on the hold frame, not mid mask-rise. | Merged: Every text holds at least max(0.833 s, 0.3 s per word) and reads at <= 17 characters/s; a 4-5 word super needs 1.5 s, not 1.03 s. [measured; Plan scores: name supers held 1.03 s for 4-5 words; three ad proof lines read over 17 cps (fix: hold 2.0-2.3 s or cut to 4-5 words); tutorial step cards rose to 1.0 s after reading at 3.5 words/s.] | eyes/readability and lint_shotlist use 0.35 s + 0.28 s per word (min 0.5 s): a second formula for the same rule; the two disagree slightly on short lines.

title: Only weights the family ships
statement: Use open-licence (OFL) families, at most 2 per piece (one display, one text), request only weights the family ships, and pin variable fonts to an exact weight; no faux bold or faux italic.
evidence: type practice in frame-design: synthetic faux-bold from a missing weight reads as a generated-design tell.
notes: Set today by: design.json type.display / type.text (license field) (a pack default outside mp plan). | Also tighten display type -0.02 to -0.035 em at 96 px and up, open mono labels +0.02 em; test every glyph (currency, diacritics) before locking a family.

title: Alternate tiny and frame-filling type
statement: Use scale contrast as rhythm: small type alternates with type that fills the frame, with the small size never below the label floor (28 px wide / 30 px tall at 1080).
evidence: A craft-only round manifesto film alternates type at 2-3% of frame height with frame-filling type; saves-strong round-3 films end on giant cropped titles or marks.
notes: 2-3% of 1080 (22-32 px) is under the read floor of 48 px wide; only labels may go that small, so eyes/readability fails body copy at the reference's size.

title: One word per shot hook
statement: A 4-5 word hook sentence is spread one word per shot across changing plates in the first 4 s, the last word larger.
evidence: Round-7 film 16 (tier A, likes 2.22%, bookmarks 2.20%, the round's strongest rates) opens this way over 4 textures.

sources.locator: Beat tables: the four tier-A films (film 16)

title: Hold typed text after it lands
statement: Text that types on holds >= 2.2 s after its last character; without that hold, typed slugs read at 18 characters/s, over the 17 cps ceiling.
evidence: The short-film scene slugs read at 18 chars/s before the 2.2 s hold was added (plan score 44 -> 78 with the beat fixes).
notes: Set today by: templates/short-film config (slug hold 2.2 s) (a pack default outside mp plan).

title: Type key text with a caret
statement: Key on-screen text is typed with a visible caret, not faded, so each word is a visible event a sound can land on.
evidence: Typed text drives time in 5 of 8 round-8 films, including 3 tier-A small-sample films (07, 08, 09).

title: Make one big word the scene
statement: Make one big word the scene with the UI small beneath it, and change the word by scramble, decode or wheel roll as a visible event for sound to hit.
evidence: 2 of 3 tier-A films: one huge word per beat with UI cards in front of its lower half; one or two short lines per card in the other.
